46   1       Introduction
47   Algebraic complexity is the study of the computation of polynomials as formal objects with
48   addition and multiplication as primitive arithmetic operations. In his seminal work, Valiant
49   [Val79] introduced two classes, VP and VNP, which are algebraic analogues of the classes P and
50   NP problem. The central question in algebraic complexity is to resolve the VP vs VNP problem
51   - prove superpolynomial size lower bounds for an explicit polynomial. We refer the reader
52   to surveys [SY10; Sap21] for a more formal treatment of the subject and especially for lower
53   bounds. For general algebraic circuits, the best known lower bound is Ωpn log nq by [BS83],
54   which is slightly better than the best known general boolean circuit lower bound of 3.1n ´ opnq
55   by [LY22]. Over the past fifty years, strong lower bounds have been proved for various restricted
56   algebraic circuits, and one particular restriction that has gained huge traction is constant depth
57   circuits. Exponential lower bounds were proved for constant-depth Boolean circuits AC0 in the
58   late 80’s by [FSS84; Hås87; Raz87; Smo87]. On the contrary, exponential lower bounds for
59   algebraic circuits have remained deceptive. In this work, we consider some further restrictions
60   on constant-depth circuits and prove lower bounds for them. We discuss more background and
61   context for our result now.
62   In the following discussion, we will always use n and d to denote the number of variables and
63   degree, respectively.

68   partial derivatives to prove an exppΩpnqq lower bound against homogeneous2 depth-3 circuits,
